Wednesday, March 12, 2014
06:00 P.M.
Minutes contain a summary of the discussions and actions taken by the City Council during a meeting. City Council meetings are video recorded and archived as a permanent record. The video recordings capture the complete proceedings of the meeting and are available for viewing on the City's website.

This portion of the agenda provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the City Council on items relating to City business and not appearing on today's agenda by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk. Comments relating to items on this evening's agenda are taken at the time the items are heard. Pursuant to the Brown Act, no action shall be taken by the City Council on public comment items. Council may refer items to the City Manager for placement on a future agenda. The maximum time allotted for each presentation is THREE MINUTES (SBMC 2.04.190). Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.

A.
CONSENT CALENDAR: (Action Items) (A.1. - A.5.)
Items listed on the Consent Calendar are to be acted in a single action of the City Council unless pulled for discussion.
Any member of the public may address the City Council on an item of concern by submitting to the City Clerk a speaker slip
(located on the back table) before the Consent Calendar is addressed.
Those items removed from the Consent Calendar by a member of the Council will be trailed to the end of the agenda,
while Consent Calendar items removed by the public will be discussed immediately after approval of
the Consent Calendar.

Recommendation: That the City Council

NOTE: The City Council shall not begin a new agenda item after 10:30 p.m. unless approved by a unanimous vote of all members present. (SBMC 2.04.070)
B.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: (B.1. - B.2.)
This portion of the agenda provides citizens an opportunity to express their views on a specific issue as required by law
after proper noticing by submitting a speaker slip (located on the back table) to the City Clerk .
After considering all of the evidence, including written materials and oral testimony,
the City Council must make a decision supported by findings and the findings must be supported by substantial evidence in the record.
An applicant or designees for a private development/business project, for which the public hearing is being held,
is allotted a total of fifteen minutes to speak, as per SBMC 2.04.210. A portion of the fifteen minutes may be saved to respond to those who speak in opposition.
All other speakers have three minutes each. Please be aware of the timer light on the Council Dais.
B.1.
Conditional Use Permit (CUP) for 305 S. Highway 101, Applicants: AT&T Mobility, Case No: 17-13-30. (File 0610-60)
1.
Conduct the Public Hearing: Open the Public Hearing, Report Council disclosures, Receive public testimony, Close the Public Hearing.
2.
Find the project exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to Section 15301 of the State CEQA Guidelines; and
3.
Adopt Resolution 2014-019 conditionally approving a CUP for a new WCF (Wireless Communication Facility) and associated equipment located on the roof of an existing commercial structure at 305 S. Highway 101, Solana Beach.
David Ott, City Manager, introduced the item.
Corey Johnson presented a PowerPoint (on file).
Mayor Campbell opened the Public Hearing.
Danielle Goldman, applicant, explained that they considered existing architectural features, proposed to the property owner to remove the green metallic sign, and incorporated existing wooden slacks to mimic the existing style.
Council and applicant discussed possibility of dividing the sector into two, making it less massive and extending coverage for the surrounding neighbors.
Council and Staff discussed discrepancies brought up by Jonathan Kramer and confirmed that the plans were revised accordingly and explanation memo provided.
Council and applicant discussed options such as moving antennas farther to the west, that reducing the size of the antenna would not offer the solution because it would require putting antenna higher up.
Council requested some alternative design and clarification on how shorter antennas could be used and how they impact the design.
Mayor Campbell stated that the hearing would be continued to May 14, 2014.
C.2.
Adopt (2nd Reading) Ordinance 447 - Use of E-Cigarettes. (File 0270-30)
Recommendation: That the City Council
1.
Adopt Ordinance 447 to include e-cigarettes and other similar devices in the definition of "smoking" so that these devices would be prohibited in all areas in the City where traditional smoking is prohibited.
Councilmember Nichols recused himself from the item due to a potential conflict of interest from having a family member in the industry.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, introduced the item.
Peggy Walker stated that she was a resident of the City and a member of the Parks and Recreation Commission. She stated that Ordinance 447 was well written, that she understood the purpose of the ordinance was to ban electronic cigarette (e-cigarette) smoking in the City, and questioned whether some of the language could be carried over the tobacco retail licensing ordinance. She asked Council if they would consider regulating the resale of e-cigarettes, and stated that many people in the drug prevention community were concerned about e-cigarettes because adolescent smoking was on the rise again. She stated that at Sunset high school in San Diego about 1 in 4 kids were using e-cigarettes, that these devices were a gateway to other drugs, that there was aggressive marketing of these devices, and that Council should consider regulating the sale by adding them to the tobacco retail permit licensing.
Judi Strang, San Dieguito Alliance for Drug Free Youth, stated that they were pleased with the ordinance, that there were 11 tobacco retailers in the city, and that 4 of them sold e-cigarettes and vapor pens. She stated that the tobacco retailer permit ordinance should be extended to include these items, that there were 4 cities in the county that added e-cigarettes/vapor pens to their tobacco retail licenses, and that there were many public venues that had added e-cigarettes to their no-smoking prohibitions.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney, stated that when the proposed ordinance was first present to Council the consensus was to move forward with an ordinance to ban e-cigarettes and similar devices in same areas of the city where smoking was prohibited, that if Council decided to move forward with Ordinance 447 it could be adopted as it was, and that if Council desired to direct staff to regulate the retail sales of e-cigarettes and other related devices it would be a separate ordinance to return for a separate introduction and adoption.
Council discussed an article in the New York Times regarding the terminology issues of definitions of the various electronic smoking devices, that it was good that the city' ordinance had a broad definition, that there was an editorial in the Union Tribune regarding that the second hand smoke from e-cigarettes were not harmful, and that the city regulating these devices was not about cultural politics.
Council and City Attorney discussed the city's current regulations for tobacco licensing under Municipal Code Section 6.17.020, that it was an added procedural step for retailers to get this permit, and permitting would allow the city to track who was selling the electronic smoking devices, and that the city could require certain information to be provided by the retailers.
Johanna Canlas, City Attorney read the title of ordinance 447.
MOTION: Moved by Zahn and seconded by Heebner to adopt Ordinance 447 and bring back another ordinance to add e-cigarettes to the city's current tobacco permitting regulations.
Motion carried 4/0/1
(Recuse:
Nichols.)

MOTION: Moved by Heebner and seconded by Nichols
